```{r setup}
here_root <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input()), ".."))
source(file.path(here_root, "R", "utils.R"))
tab <- function(name) read.csv(file.path(TAB_DIR, name))
figp <- function(f) file.path(FIG_DIR, f)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

This document tests two hypotheses for the four major Ashkenazi maternal founders
**K1a1b1a, K1a9, K2a2a, N1b2**:

- **[H1] European origin** (Costa et al. 2013): assimilated prehistoric European women.
- **[H2] Levantine origin** (Behar et al. 2006; Livni & Skorecki 2025): Near Eastern founders.

It uses the Livni-Skorecki branching / founder-vs-host model framework and adds
a phylogeographic + ancient-DNA analysis of an enriched, deduplicated
Mitotree+GenBank dataset. Behar and Costa records are provenance flags within
the dataset, not separate sample tables.

> To regenerate every table and figure, run `Rscript run_all.R` from the project
> root (after `python3 scripts/00_extract_data.py`). This document reads the
> pre-computed outputs.

## Data set

```{r dataset}
knitr::kable(tab("00_enriched_dedup_summary.csv"))
```

## Module A -- Branching-process (founder vs host) model

Galton-Watson lineage extinction: after ~27 generations (the founder event
dated to ~1325 CE at 26 years per matrilineal generation) a founder leaves
exactly one descendant with probability below 0.2% across the plausible
growth range (Livni-Skorecki Table 1).

```{r A-table1}
knitr::kable(tab("A_table1_single_descendant.csv"))
```

The fast PGF/FFT implementation is checked against a slower direct-convolution
implementation:

```{r A-audit}
knitr::kable(tab("A_branching_math_audit.csv"))
```

![Single-descendant probability](`r figp("A1_single_descendant.png")`)

Founder lineages are seen in multiple copies; absorbed (convert) lineages appear
as singletons.

![Founder vs absorbed detectability](`r figp("A2_detection_curves.png")`)

Empirical founder counts are computed from the enriched deduped dataset:

```{r A-absorption}
knitr::kable(tab("A_mitotree_founder_summary.csv")[, c(
  "founder", "modern_count", "modern_frequency", "ancient_count",
  "distinct_modern_haplogroups", "known_country_count"
)])
```

Absorption is estimated from the enriched reference set's singleton fraction
with the Behar 2006 Ashkenazi sample as the lineage-specific anchor. Note the
singleton fraction is strongly a function of sample size and clade-label depth
rather than of absorption (see `A_absorption_identifiability.csv`), so the two
estimates are comparable only at equal n and equal resolution:

```{r A-absorption-estimate}
knitr::kable(tab("A_absorption_estimate.csv"))
```

![Founder counts](`r figp("A3_mitotree_founder_frequencies.png")`)

The "Euro-Levantine" reconciliation is model-disfavored under the
Livni-Skorecki scenario (probability about 1.5% for >=3 major founders, or 5.3%
with a Dirichlet-derived rather than assumed major-frequency probability), but this is
a model sensitivity result rather than an empirical Mitotree measurement:

![Euro-Levantine feasibility](`r figp("A6_euro_levantine.png")`)

## Module B -- Phylogeography (ape + pegas)

Parent clades retain a Near Eastern signal in modern samples with known country,
but modern country is diaspora-biased and is not interpreted as origin:

![Regional composition of parent clades](`r figp("B1_parentclade_region_props.png")`)

The Costa et al. "solely European nesting" claim is not robust for K1a after
sample-size control. K2a and N1b remain mixed, so this is not a blanket proof:

![Rarefaction](`r figp("B6_rarefaction.png")`)

![Nesting of K1a1b1a](`r figp("B2_nesting_K1a1b1a.png")`)

Published non-Jewish rarity benchmark (not the analysis set):

```{r B-table7}
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(REFERENCE, "table7_nonjewish_freq.csv")))
```

![Non-Jewish rarity](`r figp("B7_nonjewish_rarity.png")`)

![Founder haplotype network](`r figp("B8_founder_haplonet.png")`)

## Module C -- Ancient DNA and diffusion (ape + adegenet)

The oldest ancient K1a records in this enriched dataset are Near Eastern
(Anatolia ~8750 BCE, Levant):

```{r C-oldest}
knitr::kable(head(tab("C_oldest_near_east.csv"), 8))
```

Ancient/historical founder-clade hits in the enriched deduped dataset:

```{r C-footprint}
knitr::kable(tab("A_mitotree_ancient_founders.csv")[, c(
  "founder", "subject", "haplogroup", "country", "year", "study"
)])
```

![Ancient timeline](`r figp("C1_ancient_timeline.png")`)

Founders coalesce recently relative to their parent clades:

```{r C-coal}
knitr::kable(tab("C_coalescence_ages.csv"))
```

![Coalescence ages](`r figp("C2_coalescence_ages.png")`)

Frequency-gradient argument: the K1a and K2a parent signatures peak in the Near
East / Anatolia (Table 3), which is supportive context but not stand-alone proof
(K1a1b1 itself is absent from the Middle East, Anatolia and Caucasus rows):

```{r C-table3}
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(REFERENCE, "table3_parent_freq.csv")))
```

![Diffusion frequencies](`r figp("C3_diffusion_frequencies.png")`)

![glPca of founder motifs](`r figp("C4_glpca_founders.png")`)

## Conclusion

The enriched deduped analysis **leans toward [H2]** for all four founders,
most strongly for K1a/K1a1b1a; it should be read as weighted evidence rather
than definitive proof. Founder clades are present in the enriched dataset, K1a's
European nesting advantage weakens after sample-size control, published
non-Jewish rarity remains a benchmark against simple European assimilation, and
historical founder-clade hits are explicitly tabulated rather than inferred from
Behar/Costa sample tables.

## Limitations

- Mitotree/GenBank is a cross-study reference set, not a random population
  sample, and its singleton fraction tracks sample size and clade-label depth
  rather than absorption, so it is not an Ashkenazi-specific estimate.
- Modern `Country` is diaspora residence, not origin; it is not used as direct
  evidence of origin.
- The public Mitotree subset is a subset of the full ~330,000 samples.
- Network / glPca use motifs reconstructed from Mitotree mutation strings.
- Branching-model equations are retained as framework; empirical counts come
  from the enriched deduped dataset.
- Built to *test* H2 vs H1; not a substitute for peer-reviewed primary analysis.

## External context

Autosomal and ancient-DNA studies frame (but do not settle) the maternal
question: Carmi et al. 2014 (severe late-medieval bottleneck, ~50/50 EU/ME
autosomal ancestry), Waldman et al. 2022 (Erfurt medieval Ashkenazi carrying
K1a1b1a/K1a9/N1b2; founder event pre-dating the 14th century), Xue et al. 2017
(European gene flow predominantly Southern European, in ≥2 events around the
founder bottleneck), Fernández et al. 2014 (deep Near Eastern Neolithic
haplogroup K at 42.8%, 6 of 14 assignable profiles), and Pallarés-Viña et al. 2026 (medieval Iberian Jewish
K1a1b1a at Tàrrega).
